Only ₱450-million has been allotted to PGH, covering just half of the ₱900-million needed to continue the Multi-Specialty Building. More urgent requests, such as the ₱1.7-billion for personnel and maintenance support and ₱1-billion for fire safety compliance, were excluded. This comes after the hospital endured three fire incidents in 2024 alone. A Manila Collegian report noted that despite a ₱260-million fire suppression allocation in 2025, the hospital merely acquired more extinguishers, leaving the promised suppression system uninstalled.

The Manila City DRRM Office has raised the BLUE ALERT as a precaution against the possible effects of the Hanging Habagat, intensified by a Low-Pressure Area (LPA) east of the country.

According to DOST-PAGASA and the city’s Resident Meteorologist, Manila may experience light to moderate, at times heavy, rains on Wednesday, August 27.

Residents, especially those near coastal and low-lying areas, are advised to stay vigilant, monitor official updates, and follow authorities’ instructions to avoid possible flooding incidents. (📷: Manila DRRM Office) | via Diann Calucin
